purpose: Test whether activation-based source-to-target channel alignment improves importance transfer on disjoint source-scoring and target-evaluation image subsets.
primary_metric: Top-10% precision for identifying the target model's truly top-10% channels by absolute loss change.

protocol.subset_selection: Reconstruct v0.6 seeded validation permutation; preserve its first 2,500 feature images; split the remaining 2,500 intervention images into the first 1,250 source-score images and last 1,250 target-evaluation images.

random_mapping_control.interpretation_note: Permutation reference only; empirical p-values do not account for dependence across layers or target seeds and are not stand-alone population significance tests.

preregistered_interpretation_rule.support_for_transfer: Directional support requires mean aligned Top-10% precision across the 9 target-layer comparisons to exceed both same-index transfer and the mean randomized-mapping control, and the layer-averaged aligned-minus-same-index difference to be positive for at least 2 of the 3 target seeds.
preregistered_interpretation_rule.not_sufficient: A single winning layer, a high activation correlation alone, or a favourable result against only one baseline is not sufficient.

limitations: The 5,000-image validation partition has previously been used for checkpoint selection; this is not a pristine external benchmark.
There are three target checkpoints; layer rows within a checkpoint are dependent and must not be treated as nine independent model replications.

The experiment tests channel-importance transfer within one dataset and one architecture, not semantic understanding, general intelligence, architecture generation, or reduced pretraining requirements.
Single-channel ablation importance is intervention-dependent and does not capture channel interactions or global causal structure.
Signed-effect correlation is secondary and may be unstable for channels with near-zero effects.
Random-mapping empirical probabilities are permutation controls, not stand-alone population-level significance tests.
